findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil residues on the following:
(i) the interior of the soda machine nozzles. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and cleaned the nozzles during the inspection until they were clean to sight and touch.
(ii) inside the ice machine. PIC was informed and instructed to clean and maintain the machine regularly to prevent contamination.
Ensure food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that several sanitizer buckets did not have a measureable amount of sanitizer in them - 0ppm (Chlorine) for the sanitizer bucket in the bar and 0ppm (quaternary ammonium) for the sanitizer buckets in the dish area. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and remade the buckets so that they measured a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer: 100ppm (Cl) for the bar sanitizer bucket made from bleach and water (1 capful of bleach to 1 gallon of water); and 200pm (quat) for the dish room sanitizer buckets (filled from the dispenser over the mop sink). Ensure that sanitizers are used per manufacturer instructions so that there is a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer for food-contact surfaces: 50-200 ppm for Chlorine-based sanitizer and 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a gap between the exterior door and door frame so that there was visible daylight along the bottom of the door. PIC was informed and will repair the door or attach a barrier to avoid entry of insects, rodents and other animals.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed an opened can of tomato purée that is stored in a cooler in its original can without a cover. Opened cans of food are not storage containers (once opened, the can itself can be source of potential contamination, especially if the food item is acidic). CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the product was removed from the cooler so that it could be repackaged in a cleanable container. Ensure that food is protected from potential contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the scoop in the chips in the server area stored with the handle touching the chips. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the scoop was moved to sit on top of the chip container where the handle does not touch the food. Since the handle is touched by bare hands it must be stored above the top of food. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-use containers stored on top of the prep cooler upright where the food-contact surfaces are exposed to debris from above. CORRECTED: Staff were informed and inverted the containers so that the food-contact surfaces were protected from contamination. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are protected by either inversion or cover from a closed shelf or packaging.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed employee washed their hands, then turned the faucet off with their newly cleaned hands. Reviewed proper handwashing procedure with PIC. Educate staff to use a barrier (such as a paper towel) to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
(i) Observed an employee washing a cooking utensil in the cookline handwashing sink. CORRECTED: The practice was interrupted and employees were educated on proper use of handwashing sinks and proper warewashing procedures. Handwashing sinks should only be used for handwashing. Nothing else. When warewashing, utensils must be washed with soapy water, rinsed with clean water, submerged in sanitizer for the manufacturer-recommended contact time, and allowed to air dry before returning to use.
(ii) The bar handsink was observed to contain ice and a spoon. CORRECTED: Staff removed the spoon from the handsink and melted the ice. Ensure handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing, no other purpose.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed containers of raw fish and beef stored over a container of tomatoes in the bottom of a prep cooler. CORRECTED: Staff moved around the food items so that the sliced fresh produce that is not getting cooked was stored above raw animal proteins that are getting cooked. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination, and that raw animal proteins are stored in order of final cooking temperature, with fish and eggs on top, pork and beef in the middle, and chicken and poultry on the bottom.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Multiple containers of whipped cream in the bar cooler were observed without date-marking. CORRECTED: Unlabeled whipped creams were labeled with the date they were opened. Any whipped cream containers that the PIC was unsure of the open date were voluntarily discarded. Ensure ready-to-eat, time/temperature controlled for safety foods are labeled with the date they were opened, and that they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening (day 1 is day of preparation or initial opening).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed some of the staff working did not have Food Handler certificates. PIC is working on scheduling training for staff. Ensure that all staff who handle or prepare food and beverages have Food Handler certificates from an accredited provider by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Observed employees missed several hand washing opportunities during the inspection:

(1) Employees did not wash hands before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with food.

(2) Employees touched gloved hands on their clothes and continued preparing foods.

The inspector educated the employees when the actions were observed. The PIC will also be continuing to educate employees about proper hand washing and glove use. Ensure that hands are always washed whenever contamination occurs.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

Immediately upon announcing my presence to staff, the container was taken back to the kitchen and the chips were dumped into a larger container on top of the single door upright cooler. Person-in-charge at first told me that these chips were fresh chips and were not being used. After some questioning regarding where the chips came from and why they were first in the dining room if they were fresh, person-in-charge state that "maybe" they are being reused. Foods previously served, even if not eaten, may NEVER be reused and served again to consumers. These foods must ALWAYS be DISCARDED after service. 

The chips were discarded during the inspection.

Complaint is founded and a follow-up is issued for 7/14/2023.
